intro: This question helps us find the best place for you to begin.

widget.instructions: Drag point P along the curve, or focus it and use the arrow keys. The tangent and its slope update as you go: the derivative gives that slope at every x.

hints.text: Move P to a few places and note the slope of the tangent. What pattern do you see?
The derivative's value at each x is the tangent's slope there. The dots mark those slopes.
Use d/dx(xⁿ) = n xⁿ⁻¹ on each term.

power-rule-forgot-multiply.text: When you differentiate x², bring the power down as a multiplier: d/dx(x²) = 2x. The dashed line uses your f′ as the tangent at P: it cuts across the curve instead of just touching it.

dropped-linear-term.text: The term {{b}}x also changes with x; its derivative is {{b}}. The dashed line uses your f′ as the tangent at P: it doesn't just touch the curve.

power-not-reduced.text: After bringing the power down, reduce it by one: d/dx(x²) = 2x¹, not 2x².

generic.text: The dashed line uses your f′(x) as the slope at P. A correct derivative gives a line that just touches the curve there. Move P and look again.

workedSolution.text: The derivative at each x is the slope of the tangent there.
So f′(x) = {{dref}}. Its graph passes through every slope dot.

steps.text: f′(x) = lim (h → 0) [f(x + h) − f(x)] ÷ h. Watch the secant become the tangent at x = 1.

power-rule-forgot-multiply.back: 2ax: bring the power down and reduce it by one.

dropped-linear-term.back: b, a constant (the slope of the line y = bx).

generic.front: What does f′(a) mean on the graph of f?
generic.back: The slope of the tangent at x = a.

accessibility.altText: Graph of f(x) = {{a}}x² {{b|signed}}x with a point P on the curve and its tangent line.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: Type an x value for P in Precise controls, or focus P and use the arrow keys.
